transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
End: 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Kaur (Zenith), Ethan Morales (Zenith), Nadia Chen (Zenith), Oliver Reed (Zenith)

Summary:
Quick lab to get Zenith engineers running Redwood SDK locally, cover auth options, show Console/Optimize suggestions, and agree next steps for a pilot. Some audio drop at ~00:18; transcription imperfect in places.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, this is Marco our SE. quick intro?
[00:10] Marco Diaz: Hi all, Marco here, I'll mostly run the lab steps and show the Optimize recommendations and the small benchmark script.
[00:20] Priya Kaur: Hey, Priya, lead ML eng at Zenith. our stack is mostly Python microservices, a Node analytics UI, and we've got internal model ops people.
[00:32] Ethan Morales: Ethan, Platform, I manage our k8s clusters and CI. we'll want to know about network and VPC options.
[00:40] Nadia Chen: Nadia, Security. SOC2 + KMS questions up front for me.
[00:46] Oliver Reed: Oliver, CTO, mostly listening but interested in latency vs cost tradeoffs.
[00:52] Lena: Great. Agenda: quick SDK install (py/ts), auth options (api key vs SSO/SAML), local docker + env vars, Console demo focusing on per-route cost breakdown, then Optimize suggestions. We'll leave time for security.

[02:12] Marco: Ok I'll share my screen; first step, pip install redwood-sdk (notes: our internal package currently named redwood-inference on pip), for TS it's @redwood/inference. Common gotcha: set REDWOOD_API_KEY vs SSO token.
[03:05] Priya: Do you recommend API keys for CI or SSO for devs?
[03:18] Marco: For CI and short-lived apps use API keys with scoped permissions; for devs and team access we recommend SSO + short token exchange via our CLI. Also RBAC in console to limit routes.
[03:46] Ethan: On network, if we do Private (VPC) how do sandbox workflows talk? we want a dev path without opening prod VPC.
[03:58] Lena: We usually spin a dedicated sandbox VPC or use Private with a jump host; for quick labs we give a hosted sandbox with IP allowlist. We'll provide the sandbox creds.

[05:20] Marco: Walkthrough - Python quickstart: create venv, pip install redwood-inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, run example generate.py. I'll paste the command in chat. Note: use python 3.10+ for best dependency compatibility.
[06:02] Priya: Any sample code for async streaming? we need streaming in our UI.
[06:17] Marco: Yes example shows streaming via callback; TS/Node example uses stream responses with event emitter. There is a small difference: Node example uses fetch-based streaming and you need node 18+ or undici.

[07:30] Marco: Now TS quickstart: npm install @redwood/inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env, import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference' and call client.createChat(...). We demoed a short snippet.
[08:05] Ethan: We use secrets in vault — how do we rotate keys?
[08:14] Marco: Rotate via Console -> API Keys; we issue short-lived keys or integrate with KMS hooking into our Private deploys. For hosted we support HS256 signed tokens or SAML-backed session to avoid long-lived keys.

[09:40] Nadia: On encryption: are requests server-side encrypted end-to-end? what about customer-owned keys?
[09:49] Lena: TLS in transit and we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private so you can manage model access keys. We'll send the KMS integration docs.

[11:00] Marco: Now Docker/local dev: we showed a minimal Dockerfile that installs the SDK and runs example server; important env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV (sandbox/prod), REDWOOD_REGION if using multi-region. For local dev use hosted sandbox key.
[12:05] Priya: Would recommend mounting token file rather than env var in Docker?
[12:14] Marco: Both work; mounting is slightly more secure in some CI setups. For k8s use secrets and RBAC.

[13:30] Marco: Console: routes view -> per-route token-level cost breakdown (tokens in/out, model used), latency percentiles, and recent regressions. We scrolled to the Optimize tab and saw recommendations: enable continuous batching with 1-50ms wait window, turn on prefix KV cache for repeated context, and suggested quantization profile for the family of models you're testing.
[14:45] Oliver: That quantization note—does it change output quality? we can't degrade throughputs.
[14:55] Marco: Good question. Quantization typically trades off some fp precision for 30-60% throughput gain; Redwood Optimize simulates quality drift on your eval set and reports expected F1/accuracy delta. We recommend canaries with A/B routes.

[16:20] Priya: Show us the Optimize explainability — how do I know suggestions are safe for client-facing chat?
[16:30] Marco: Optimize attaches a score and estimated unit cost savings; it also runs your prompt set through model variants and flags regressions. We demoed a small eval harness in the repo that runs prompt sets and collects BLEU/F1 or custom metrics.

[18:00] Marco: Example command: redwood-eval --prompts prompts.json --model redwood-small-q4 --report out/report.json, it will compare to baseline.
[18:20] Priya: Nice. Where's the repo link?
[18:25] Lena: I'll send the sandbox repo link in the follow-up — link in chat: https://git.redwood.example/zenith-sandbox (note: placeholder).

[19:40] Ethan: For pilot we want 95th percentile latency under 250ms for 64-token responses, any idea if hosted will achieve that?
[19:52] Marco: Hosted can often hit that for small-contexts on optimized kernels; for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated GPU pools and pin model variants. We can run a 24-hour benchmark with your prompts to validate.

[21:10] Nadia: Security checklist: SOC2 type II? audit logs? SSO/SAML?
[21:18] Lena: We are SOC2 compliant and provide audit logs, SAML SSO, OIDC, RBAC. For Private we can extend logs to your SIEM. We'll attach our compliance pack.

[23:00] Marco: Now quick snippet of running the benchmark locally: python bench.py --model redwood-base --prompt-file sample_prompts.json --concurrency 8. We also demoed a small k6 script for concurrency emulation.
[24:05] Priya: What's the best way to test KV cache behavior?
[24:14] Marco: Use repeated prefix prompts and measure token compute; Optimize will show cache hit rates per-route. Locally you can simulate by sending repeated warmup requests and then measuring tail latency.

[26:00] Oliver: Regarding data residency—if we need EU-only, can Redwood pin region for hosted?
[26:10] Lena: Yes we have region pinning for hosted and Private deployments inside EU; Dedicated can be provisioned in specific regions.

[27:30] Marco: We hit a couple of small environment hiccups: Node version mismatch (they had node 16 previously) and pip deps. I posted the exact compatibility table in chat.

[29:00] Priya: For the TS SDK, do you have typings and TS examples for function-calling?
[29:10] Marco: Yes, full typings and function-calling examples included; one note: ensure your schema is stable; we showed an example with structured output type hints.

[31:15] Ethan: Any rate-limiting recommended defaults when starting a pilot?
[31:25] Lena: Start with conservative quotas, like 10 requests/sec per route, and then let Optimize suggest batching to reduce per-token costs. Console will show throttled requests and suggested quota increases.

[33:00] Marco: We also demoed rollouts: create a canary route that points to the quantized variant and a fallback to full precision. If errors spike, automatic fallback triggers.

[34:40] Nadia: For audits, do you expose raw request logs with redaction?
[34:48] Lena: Yes logs are available with PII redaction hooks; in Private you can keep logs in your cloud storage. We'll include sample log schema in the security pack.

[36:00] Marco: Live troubleshooting: Priya ran into an auth error '401 token not found' — turned out REDWOOD_API_KEY was set in process but not in Docker image. Common Docker-env gotcha.
[36:25] Priya: yup that was me — thanks.

[38:00] Marco: We briefly discussed cost modeling: per-token cost shown in console, and Optimize will estimate savings from batching+quantization. Example: batching 8x reduced token cost by ~40% in our demo.

[40:10] Oliver: How do we handle model rollbacks?
[40:18] Marco: Rollouts support canary + automatic rollback on latency or quality regressions; the Console shows diffs and you can pin the stable version.

[42:00] Lena: Ok nearing the end — let's recap next steps: we'll send sandbox creds, sample repo, security pack, and a benchmark script. Zenith will share prompts and confirm pilot dates.

[43:15] Priya: For the benchmark script, can you include guidance on measuring 95/99 pctl and output quality?
[43:25] Marco: Yes we'll include k6 + redwood-eval integration and a small eval harness that computes custom metrics.

[45:00] Nadia: One more on compliance: please include encryption-at-rest details for hosted and the KMS integration checklist.
[45:10] Lena: Will do.

[46:30] Ethan: For the pilot environment, can we have a dedicated pool on a trial basis?
[46:40] Lena: We can provision a short-term dedicated pool for benchmarking — that would be part of the pilot proposal.

[48:00] Marco: I'll draft the benchmark config templates: concurrency profiles, prompt mix, token budgets.

[49:15] Oliver: If we like results, timeline to scale beyond pilot? we need procurement involvement.
[49:25] Lena: Typical path is pilot -> commitment for Dedicated or Private within 4–8 weeks depending on procurement. We'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.

[50:50] Priya: Thanks all. any blockers on our side? we'll upload prompt sets and schedule pilot.
[51:05] Lena: Great, we'll follow up with links and the demo recording. Thanks everyone.
[51:30] Marco: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
